- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum (e.g., sentiment change > -0.67 or news volume drops to 0), model tends to overcorrect or overshoot downward — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overreacts with a prolonged upward bias — cap forecast slope after peak to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days) but price declines, model underreacts — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match sentiment decay.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a 1–2% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion patterns.
- If news volume is 0 for 2+ consecutive days, model tends to drift — apply a 0.5–1.5% downward correction to avoid overconfidence in stagnant sentiment.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term volatility in high-sentiment periods — reduce forecast variance by 10–20% when sentiment >0.75.
